title: St. Louis, Curly Lozano and the Karubas
summary: Too poor to visit brother in St. Louis; asked about Curly Lozano and Mike Karuba.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Oh yeah. What about St. Louis? Did you go up to St. Louis to see your brother there?

No. That was a long trip then. No. It wasn't possible. We were too poor for one thing. From the time I was twelve years old I guess I worked all the time. My family hadn't lost everything that they own. I bought my own clothes all the time and worked and went to school.
Did you know Curly Lozano over on the golf course? Oh yes sir.

Where was he from? I can't say. But he was over there. Yeah. You know the Karuba family, Mike and all, you know Mike. I know Mike, yes. Well I, well there was a family of Karubas that lived in Long Beach and I think Mike must be part of that family. Mm-hmm. I couldn't say. And I played a job with Mike not too long ago with Val Barbaro.

Yeah. But Curly, you knew Curly over there and did you play with him? No. See, I just was curious about that. Well you're talking about your work and everything. Did you, when did you start tuning pianos?
